# 03 — UI

Implements the tool section of `docs/campaign-plan.md` (interaction model v3). Six pages, open-anytime, pull-based, **desktop-only**. Beautiful and fun are requirements, not decoration. Single-user personal tool.

**Interaction model (binding):** no rituals, no decision docs, no accept/override ceremony, **no notifications of any kind**. Louis opens the tool whenever he wants, presses **Refresh**, reads the intelligence, and makes every decision himself. The tool informs; it never pushes, reminds, or nags. His picks are logged automatically each GW via his FPL team ID (public post-deadline endpoint, no login stored; the ID is a config value requested once at setup) and predicted vs actual is tracked across the season.

**Platform (binding):** designed for a large display only. Wide cards, generous whitespace, huge display text, medium body text, never cramped. No mobile layouts, no responsive compromises, no PWA. Minimum design target ~1440px wide.

**Access (binding):** no auth, no password gate. Personal tool at an unguessable URL. The browser holds only a read-only anon key; all writes and all metered actions go through server routes (doc 02 §7). Because there is no login wall, the Analyst route carries a server-side monthly spend cap — flagged here once so the "no gate" choice never becomes an open-ended bill.

**Cost rule (binding):** every number on every page — squad scoring, projections, evaluations, comparisons — is computed internally (SQL + arithmetic over stored engine output). **Zero AI calls in any evaluation path.** AI spend is exactly two things: the Haiku presser pipeline (doc 02 §6) and **the Analyst** (§4 below, doc 02 §9) — which fires only on an explicit press, never on a schedule.

**Consistency notes (explicit, not silently resolved):**
- The campaign plan requires the Odds API credit counter and pipeline health to stay visible. These live in the **status sheet** opened from the freshness strip (§2.0), which also carries the Analyst spend meter.
- Rank-vs-pace tracking and the GW19/GW28 gate markers fold into the **My Team card expansion** on the Dashboard (§3.1).

---

## 1. Design direction

**FPL-official-but-elevated.** Premier League DNA — the purple, the electric green — executed as a premium dark product rather than a broadcast graphic. On a big screen the luxury cue is space: a wide fixed grid, huge numerals, air around everything.

**Theme tokens:**

- Background `--bg #0D0014`, raised `--bg-raise #16021F`; cards `--card #1E0630` with 1px `--line #3A1150` borders; radius 24px cards, 999px chips.
- Text `--text #F7F4FA`, `--dim #B4A3C6`.
- Accents, one job each: `--green #00FF85` (PL green — positive, projections, primary actions), `--cyan #04F5FF` (informational, links), `--pink #E90052` (PL pink — risk, brutal fixtures), `--amber #FFB454` (staleness only).
- Type — **FINAL, LOCKED (Louis, 23 Jul):** exactly three fonts, strict roles, minimum rendered size 12px anywhere in the product. **Michroma** for identity: the page title (ALL CAPS), hero numbers, team codes, the wordmark — never lowercase running text. **Outfit** for everything read: card titles (bold, sentence case), player names, body, buttons, the toolbar. **Martian Mono 800** for everything counted: prices, points, xP, ranks, FDR, deadlines, spend, micro-labels — heavy, wide, and unmissable. No fourth font, ever. Navigation/controls rail sits on the **right** edge.
- **Legibility rules (binding, all screens):** text is white only — full `#FFFFFF` for primary, `rgba(255,255,255,0.85)` secondary, `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)` tertiary floor. **No purple-blended greys, ever.** Body weight floor is 600 (Outfit 600/700/800); nothing thin anywhere. Text placed over the pitch carries a dark backing or text shadow. **Numeric plate rule:** numbers in rows and cards sit centred (both axes) on their own dark plates (#0D0014 on raised rows, #16021F on cards) with even padding — never raw on the row, never overlapping.
- **Colour restraint:** green = projections, positives, primary actions. Pink = risk and brutal fixtures. **Cyan = links and at most one eyebrow accent — never running text or data**, it fails contrast on the dark purple at small sizes. Neutral data defaults to white.
- **The pitch (binding):** anywhere a squad or lineup renders, it renders on an **FPL-style green pitch** — striped grass, white markings (centre arc, penalty box, six-yard box), goal end at the bottom, forwards at the top, GK at the bottom, and the bench on a dark bar at the foot of the grass. Kit shirts on the grass, names/prices on dark backing plates.
- **Case system (deliberate, branded):** labels/eyebrows = ALL-CAPS mono with wide tracking; page and card titles = sentence case in display weight; buttons = ALL-CAPS; body = sentence case with full stops. No mixed-case drift, no developer-style labels anywhere in the UI — every visible string is user language.
- **Kit shirts:** every player in the product is represented by a simple shirt glyph (SVG template — body colour + sleeve colour, no club badges) filled with the club's colours. Clubs with similar palettes get deliberately distinct hues per their real branding (e.g. Liverpool #C8102E all-red, Man Utd #DA291C with black sleeves, Arsenal #EF0107 with white sleeves, Forest #E53233). One colour map, used everywhere a player appears: pitch views, table rows, candidate lists.
- Signature element: the **projection fan** (p5→p95 gradient band, bright median tick) — the one visual device for uncertainty, everywhere a projection appears.
- **Alignment rule:** chips, badges and counters are fixed-height flex containers with centred content and `leading-none` — no baseline drift, ever. Off-centre elements are defects.
- Motion: sparing — Refresh spin, hero count-ups, drawer slides. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Component stack:** Next.js App Router, Tailwind, shadcn/ui primitives (drawer, tabs, slider, toast), visx for fans/distributions, Recharts for simple lines. Desktop pointer interactions (hover states, drag) are first-class.

**Navigation:** fixed **right rail** (240px): wordmark + RANK ONE, six items — **Dashboard · Squad · Builder · Players · Analysis · News** — REFRESH and ASK buttons, and the freshness block (two lines: ALL DATA FRESH · Updated n min ago · view status) at the bottom. Content area max-width 1480px, centred, px-10.

## 2. Global elements

### 2.0 Rail controls, header, data status (every page)

```
┌ rail ─────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ FPL.              │ │  FPL 2026/27 · CAMPAIGN                       │
│ RANK ONE          │ │  Dashboard            GW8 DEADLINE · SAT     │
│                   │ │  (display title)      11:00 · 2D 14H LEFT    │
│ Dashboard         │ │                                               │
│ Squad             │ │  [ stat strip — §3.1 ]                        │
│ Builder           │ │  [ quadrants ]                                │
│ Players           │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│ Analysis          │
│ News              │
│                   │
│ [⟳ REFRESH]       │  ← primary controls live in the rail,
│ [✦ ASK · ~$0.10]  │    left side, always in the same place
│                   │
│ ● ALL DATA FRESH  │  ← plain-language status; click opens
│ Updated 2m ago    │    the Data status panel
└───────────────────┘
```

- **The rail carries the controls.** Refresh and Ask are fixed at the left, under the navigation — one place, every page, never competing with content. The header carries only identity (eyebrow + page title) and the deadline chip.
- **Refresh** hits the on-demand endpoint (doc 02 §8): re-pulls FPL API data (prices, injuries, ownership, fixtures, live points during matches) and recomputes derived aggregates. Debounced 60s server-side; spin → "Updated just now" + a plain-language toast. **Odds are never refreshed here** — scheduled pulls only, to protect credits.
- **Ask** opens the Analyst drawer (§4), estimated cost on the button.
- **Data status (no developer labels):** the rail shows one plain line — "ALL DATA FRESH · updated 2m ago" (amber + named source if anything is stale). Clicking opens the **Data status panel**, written in user language: "Player prices, injuries & ownership — 2 min ago", "Betting market (match odds) — Thu 06:00, next pull Fri 09:00", "Expected goals data — Wed 05:00", "Press conference signals — Fri 08:00", "Analyst spend this month — $2.84 of $8.00 cap", plus one line explaining the odds schedule. Heartbeat/credit/version detail lives one level deeper for debugging, never on the surface.
- **Deadline chip:** `GW8 DEADLINE · SAT 11:00 · 2D 14H LEFT` — passive information, never a notification.

## 3. Pages

### 3.1 DASHBOARD

Big chunky header, generous padding, then a **stat strip** and a fixed 2×2 quadrant grid — sized so the strip and all four quadrants land in one desktop viewport. Dense with information, never cramped: space comes from tight, aligned rows, not oversized elements.

**Post-GW review module (C-14):** appears on the Dashboard the morning after settlement (Monday audit), collapsed to one line — `GW7 REVIEW · predicted 58 → actual 71 · captaincy ✓ · 1 component miss` — expanding to per-player predicted-vs-actual plates, the captaincy outcome, and the named engine component that missed. Every expansion is already written to `analyst_memory`, so reading it costs nothing and the Analyst has seen it.

**Season bar** (one element, not floating tiles): a single slim card divided into six segments by hairlines, all mono — `BANK £1.3 | TEAM VALUE £101.2 | FREE TRANSFERS 2 | CHIPS SET 1 4/4 → GW19 | GW AVERAGE 54 | OVERALL RANK 214,381 ▲96k`. Instant answers to the questions asked most often, read as one unit under the header. **Every tile is a button** — bank/value/transfers/chips open Squad; average/rank open the season modal.

**Season modal** (click the My Team hero or the rank tile): predicted vs actual for every GW with per-GW deltas, season totals, and the overall rank line against the #1 pace gate. The pick tracker's payoff view.

**Live state:** the My Team card carries a FINAL/LIVE toggle. During a gameweek, LIVE shows the live score, per-player live points (dashes for those yet to play), an "N TO PLAY" chip, and Refresh pulls the latest. Captain points always render on a **neon light blue ×2 plate** (`#3ECBFF`, dark text); all other player points are white (faded if 0 minutes) — no colour coding on the pitch.

```
[ BANK ][ TEAM VALUE ][ FREE TRANSFERS ][ CHIPS ][ GW AVG ][ OVERALL RANK ]
┌───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐
│ TRENDING PLAYERS              │ MY TEAM · GW7 FINAL           │
│ 👕 Semenyo BOU·M·£7.3         │  PROJECTED 58 → ACTUAL 71 +13 │
│    NEXT BRE (H) · xP 5.3      │        [FWD row]              │
│    ▌12▌15▌11         38/3GW   │        [MID row]              │
│ 👕 Gyökeres ARS·F·£9.4        │        [DEF row]              │
│    NEXT bou (A) · xP 6.4 …    │        [GK row]   ← GK bottom │
├───────────────────────────────┤  BENCH GK Sels·1 Timber IN·   │
│ FIXTURE SWINGS                │        2 O'Brien·3 Larsen     │
│ ARS EASING 3.8→2.4            │  AUTO-SUB · Timber ▸ Van Dijk │
│  bou WOL eve SUN bre          ├───────────────────────────────┤
│  YOU OWN · Raya·Gabriel·Saka  │ PLAYERS · TOP SCORERS         │
│ CHE BRUTAL 2.6→4.4            │ [ALL][GK][DEF][MID][FWD]      │
│  YOU OWN · Palmer             │ 👕 Haaland  xP 7.8 · 61 · 4.3 │
└───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Top-left — Trending Players:** strongest back-to-back form. Row = kit shirt, player, club/pos/price, **next fixture + xP chip** (the actionable bit: form plus what it's worth next week), last-3 mini bars, streak total. Click → player profile.
- **Top-right — My Team:** projected vs actual, huge, with a perfectly centred delta chip. Pitch graphic in kit shirts with points per shirt, rows ordered **forwards at the top, goalkeeper at the bottom**. Below the pitch, the **bench in substitution order** (GK, 1, 2, 3); auto-subbed players are highlighted `IN` with the outfield starter they replace dimmed and marked `0′ OUT`, plus a one-line `AUTO-SUB` note. Auto-sub display follows real FPL logic: 0-minute starters replaced by the first bench outfielder that keeps the formation legal (min 3 DEF / 2 MID / 1 FWD); GK swaps only with GK; the actual total shown is the post-autosub total. Click → season expansion: predicted-vs-actual per GW, rank trajectory vs the #1 pace line, GW19/GW28 gate markers.
- **Bottom-left — Fixture Swings:** direction, next-5 opponent FDR chips, avg-FDR before→after, and a **`YOU OWN · …` line per team** so every swing is immediately actionable against the current squad. Click a team → its players on the Players page.
- **Bottom-right — Player database preview:** top players with inline position filter; columns `PLAYER · GW xP · PTS · £M · PTS/£` (kit shirt per row). Footer opens the full Players page.

### 3.2 SQUAD BUILDER (the flagship — pitch-first)

Used for the initial GW1 squad from zero, then every Wildcard and Free Hit. **The pitch is the centrepiece and the starting point**: a full FPL-style green pitch with 15 slots (XI in the chosen structure, forwards top, GK bottom, bench bar on the grass). Choices flow from the pitch. Two tabs — **BUILD** and **DRAFTS** — with the **live feedback panel** fixed as the right column at all times.

```
[ BUILD ]  [ DRAFTS (2) ]        [SAVE AS DRAFT] [£12.4 LEFT]   ┌ FEEDBACK ──────────┐
                                                                │ ① PROJECTED POINTS │
[3-5-2 EV 8.4] [4-4-2 EV 7.9] [3-4-3 EV 7.1]  ← structure      │   287 · slider 1–12│
──────────────────────────────────────────────                 │ ② CAPTAINCY        │
│░░░░░░░░░ GREEN PITCH ░░░░░░░░░░│  FWD  [Haaland][+FWD]        │   Haaland · 41%    │
│░ white markings, striped grass│  MID  [Saka][Semenyo][+][+]  │ ③ RISK FLAGS  1    │
│░ empty slots = dashed + PICK  │  DEF  [Gabriel][+][+]        │   Hall — doubt 0.7 │
│░ goal end at the bottom       │  GK   [Raya]                 │ ④ STRUCTURE        │
│░ BENCH bar on the grass       │  BENCH [Sels][+][+][+]       │   spread + bench   │
──────────────────────────────────────────────                 └────────────────────┘
RANKED FOR 3-5-2 · MID — PICK 5   ← candidates for the clicked slot
Saka £10.8 ▓▓▓▓ xP 6.1 [ADD] · Semenyo £7.3 ▓▓▓ xP 5.3 [ADD] · …
```

- **Flow:** pick a structure (chips ranked by strategy-study evidence, each with its score) → click any empty slot on the pitch → ranked candidates for that position appear below, inside the structure's budget envelope → ADD fills the slot; click a filled shirt to remove. XI fills first; extra picks per position drop to the bench bar automatically. Free assembly is inherent — any slot, any legal player — so no separate "free build" mode exists.
- **Legality live:** budget (£100.0), 3-per-club, and position limits are enforced on every ADD with a plain-language toast; bank is always visible next to SAVE.
- **DRAFTS — saved squads only.** The tab holds nothing but squads Louis has saved from the pitch via SAVE AS DRAFT (named, up to three kept). Empty state invites the first save. With 2–3 saved: side-by-side comparison on the exact four readouts plus cost and structure, best value per row in green; SET PLAN star marks the plan of record (`is_plan_of_record`); LOAD puts a draft back on the pitch; delete removes it. The GW1 pure/moderate/spicy variants are generated by B-16 **as three saved drafts here** — they arrive as Louis's drafts, not as pre-filled furniture.
- **Feedback panel — exactly four readouts, all internal, instant, free:**
  1. **Projected points** with a horizon slider, this GW up to 12 (sums stored per-GW projections with fixture adjustment; fan from stored covariances).
  2. **Captaincy strength** — best in-squad captain EV + P(12+).
  3. **Risk flags** — minutes/injury count + named list from `minutes_forecasts` + `presser_signals`.
  4. **Structure** — budget spread across positions + bench quality score.
- **All 7 formations** as chips (3-5-2 · 4-4-2 · 3-4-3 · 4-3-3 · 5-3-2 · 4-5-1 · 5-4-1), each with its strategy-study evidence score; the highest carries a TOP badge.
- **Captain & vice:** click any shirt for a menu — make captain (green C), make vice (white V), remove from squad. The feedback panel uses the chosen captain (tagged SET) or falls back to the best option (tagged AUTO). No CLEAR button; removal lives in this menu.
- **Drag and drop everywhere possible (desktop):** drag a bench player onto a starter of the same position to swap XI↔bench; drag within the bench to reorder. Same-position swaps only.
- **AUTO-COMPLETE:** one press fills every remaining slot by pure arithmetic — best xP affordable while reserving minimum prices for the other empty slots. Free, instant, no AI.
- **Player rows** (modal + browser): kit, name, price, **NEXT fixture** (uppercase = home, lowercase = away), xP bar, and the neon light blue VALUE tag. Full filter set: club, max price, sort (xP / price / value / name), HIDE FLAGGED, HIDE IN SQUAD.

### 3.3.1 Multi-GW transfer planner (C-15)

Extension of the transfer plan card on the Squad page. Moves are planned 1–4 GWs ahead and stored in `transfer_plans`:
- Each move row carries its target GW; the card groups rows by GW with the banked-FT count shown per GW on the path to the 5-cap (2026/27 rules).
- Projected gain per move = Δ(ep over the horizon from that GW) − hit cost, from `projections`; the plan total nets everything.
- **Conflict flags:** a planned move collides when its IN player has `rise_risk = high` before the planned GW (price likely to move first) or when the OUT player's fixture run swings easier before the sale — both render as a pink flag chip on the row with a one-line reason.
- Everything stays informational: acting happens in the official app, same as the single-GW card.

### 3.4 PLAYERS

Full database. Filters: position, price band, team, availability. Sorting: projected points, total points, form, **value (points per £m)**, EO, price change. Dense desktop table, fan per row, columns aligned in mono.

**Row columns (locked, Louis):** PRICE · APPS · GOALS · ASSISTS · CS · PTS · OWN% · **VALUE** — value renders as a neon light blue tag (`#3ECBFF`, white 800 text) — the hue shared with the captain/×2 accent. xP and the mini form bars ride alongside. The labelled colour-banded form bar chart (points above each bar; colour-coded red ≤3, amber 4–7, green 8–12, light blue 13+ super-hauls) is the standard component: labelled large in profiles and Trending, unlabelled mini in dense rows.

**Raw data presented properly — no dumbed-down commentary, no tooltips explaining basics.** Column headers are the stat names; the reader is assumed expert.

Player profile (right drawer): projection distribution (large fan), next-6 fixtures with per-fixture xP chips, form trend, minutes risk (P(start), sub patterns, presser signal), price + ownership context.

### 3.4.3 Set-piece matrix (C-13)

A **SET PIECES** view chip on the Players page (next to the position tabs) swaps the table for the 20-team matrix: one row per club — penalty taker (rank 1 + understudy), direct-FK taker, primary corner taker — from `set_piece_duty`, each cell a name plate with a green dot when the player is in the squad and a staleness tint when `as_of` predates the last presser sweep. Row click opens the taker's profile. Penalty duty is the most concentrated point source in the game; this is its dedicated surface.

### 3.5 ANALYSIS

The deep page. Sections, each a wide card with chart + written finding, produced by the strategy study (ticket B-18) and refreshed monthly:
- **Formations/structures:** best-performing structures historically and this season (points and pts/£ by formation, top-10k adoption).
- **Value by position and price band:** pts-per-£ curves — where the market misprices.
- **Budget structures:** how high-finishing squads spread budget (premium count, bench spend vs return).
- **Template vs differential:** returns of high-EO vs low-EO picks by rank band.
- **Top-manager behaviour:** patterns from community-scraped top-10k pick archives + champions' season summaries (chip timing, transfer cadence, captaincy discipline).

All findings live here **as data** — evidence scores, effect sizes, source season ranges — and **set the Guided builder's defaults** (Step 1 cites these cards).

### 3.5.1 Analysis deep-links (routed actions, binding)

The two study interactions are real routed actions with pre-set state, not decoration (ticket C-16):
- **Structure row → Builder:** clicking a shape in the formations study navigates to Squad Builder with that structure pre-selected and the BUILD tab active.
- **Value cell → Players:** clicking a heatmap cell navigates to Players with position + price-band filters pre-applied.
Both fire a confirmation toast naming what was loaded. Implemented and proven in `fpl-app-mockup.jsx`; the real build carries the same state through URL params so links are shareable.

### 3.4.1 Player profile drawer — full contents (FM-desktop depth)

480px right drawer, density through layout, never cramming. Top to bottom:
1. Header: kit, name, club · pos · price · own% · in-squad flag; risk banner if flagged; **LOW SAMPLE · PROMOTED PRIORS ACTIVE UNTIL GW10** chip for promoted-club players while `prior_blend > 0`.
2. GW projection: hero xP + P10–median–P90 fan.
3. Next 6 fixtures: FDR chips with per-fixture xP under each.
4. Form: last-5 labelled bars + 5GW total plate.
5. Minutes block: P(start) (pink < 70), avg mins, apps; risk detail line.
6. **Underlying · season:** xG, xA, G−xG plates; finishing read line when |G−xG| ≥ 1.2 ("RUNNING HOT — REGRESSION RISK" pink / "UNDERLYING BEATS OUTPUT — BUY SIGNAL" green); **home/away xP** plates; **price trajectory** £start → £now with delta colour. Alongside: **Understat shot map** (mini half-pitch SVG, green dot = goal, white = shot).
7. Season counters: PTS / G / A / CS + value tag.
8. Action footer: owned players get SELL & REPLACE IN SQUAD (routes to the Squad replace modal); unowned players get PLAN A TRANSFER FOR HIM (routes to Squad with an instructional toast — the replace list already ranks him). Every profile ends in an action; no dead ends.

The News page opens with a **summary strip** in the season-bar tile pattern: SIGNALS TODAY · YOUR PLAYERS AFFECTED (pink when > 0) · PRICE MOVES TONIGHT · CUP-WATCHER.

### 3.4.2 Player comparison (C-11) + Differential screener (C-12)

- **COMPARE** toggle on the Players controls row enters compare mode: row clicks select up to 3 players (green border), a floating bar (bottom-centre, above toast level) shows chips + COMPARE button (needs ≥ 2). The comparison drawer shows kit-header columns, then plate rows — price, GW xP, next, 5GW pts, season pts, G·A, xG·xA, finishing, own%, P(start), home/away xP, value — with the **best value per row highlighted green** (own% best = lowest: differential edge), and **overlaid projection fans** on a shared axis (one colour per player, P10 band + median tick + P90 label).
- **DIFFERENTIALS** toggle is a one-click preset: own% ≤ 15 and xP ≥ 4.5, table intact and re-sortable; the build version ranks by the xP-vs-EO gap using `eo_snapshots.top10k_proxy`.

### 3.6 NEWS

Kept off the dashboard by design. Reverse-chron feed with type filters:
- **Injuries/pressers:** signal chips (`out/doubt/rested/confirmed` + confidence) from the Haiku pipeline, grouped by club.
- **Price changes:** last night's risers/fallers; tonight's rise-risk flags for players in the squad or drafts — surfaced here, never pushed.
- **Structure news:** cup-watcher blank/double confirmations, deadline schedule changes, ruleset updates.

### 3.7 Mockup files

**Fiction convention:** the standalone Builder mockup runs the GW1 pre-season context (GW1 deadline chip, AUG Analyst spend); every other standalone and the fully linked app run the unified GW8 / OCT fiction.

`mockups/` holds seven approved prototypes: one standalone file per screen (dashboard, builder, squad, players, analysis, news) and `fpl-app-mockup.jsx` — the fully linked six-page app with working cross-navigation (season bar → Squad, trending/news → player profiles, profile → sell & replace, fixture swings → filtered Players, analysis structures → Builder, value cells → filtered Players). The linked app is the reference for the real build's routing and state shape.

## 4. The Analyst (on-demand AI, every screen)

An **Ask** action sits in the header of every page. It fires **only on an explicit press — never scheduled** — and the button itself displays the estimated cost per call. Model: an OpenRouter model. Full pipeline spec, payload contents, memory schema, and the verbatim system prompt live in doc 02 §9; the UI contract is:

```
✦ ASK · ~$0.10  →  right drawer:
┌ THE ANALYST ────────────────────────────────┐
│ context: Squad page · GW7 · memory: 14 recs │
│ [ optional question field ]                 │
│ [ ASK — $~0.10 ]  [ COPY ANALYST PAYLOAD ]  │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ (dense streamed response …)                 │
│ THE LEVER: …                                │
│ this call: $0.09 · month: $2.84 / cap $8.00 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Context assembly is code, per call** (shared payload builder): current squad + bank + chips; full current-GW projections with distributions; fixture and odds context; relevant strategy-study findings; the screen asked from; the Analyst's MEMORY records.
- **Memory:** the drawer shows how many memory records were loaded; the Analyst's own conclusions are written back and fed into future calls. Memory lives in the database, not in any chat.
- **Cost honesty:** estimated cost before the press, actual cost after, month-to-date spend vs the server-side cap in the footer and on the status sheet.
- **Copy Analyst Payload:** assembles the *identical* context as formatted text on the clipboard for pasting into Louis's own Claude Project — the zero-API-cost path. Both routes share the same payload builder, so the two never drift.

## 5. Fun, explicitly

- Refresh has a satisfying spin-and-settle; hero numbers count up; a green flash when actual beats projected.
- Draft comparisons animate their diffs; the chip expiry wall is visually a wall; the Analyst drawer streams like a terminal.
- Empty states invite action ("No drafts yet — start in Guided"); errors say what happened and what to do; nothing apologises, nothing nags.
